maya_customer: Hey team — we have a customer-facing bug: when using structured JSON mode over streaming (SSE) the payload occasionally ends mid-object inside an array. Client libs fail to parse. Started ~2026-03-16 22:00 UTC after a deploy. Repro below, minimal curl + observed stream.

alex_support: Thanks @maya_customer — can you paste the exact curl you used and a raw stream dump? Also which region / deployment (hosted/dedicated/private)?

maya_customer: Using hosted in us-west-2. CURL we used:

```bash
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"open-structured-1","mode":"json","prompt":"generate_list"}' \
  https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/streams/generate
```

Raw stream (trimmed):
```
event: message
data: {"items":[{"id":1,"text":"alpha"},{"id":2,"text":"beta"},{"id":3,"text":"gamma"}

event: message
data: {"items":[{"id":1,"text":"alpha"},{"id":2,"text":"beta"},{"id":3,"text":"gam
```

You can see the second HTTP chunk ends in the middle of the string "gamma" and the connection closes shortly afterwards. Consumers see JSON parse errors (unexpected end of input).

ingest-proxy-bot: alert: proxy_conn_closed 1958000002 route=/v1/streams/generate peer=203.0.113.14 reason=reset_by_peer

karim_eng: That's helpful. Two quick possibilities: 1) upstream closes TCP early (proxy/nginx) 2) chunked transfer or keepalive buffer/flush on the edge is splitting event payloads unexpectedly and client isn't reassembling. Do you have reverse-proxy logs (x-request-id) or x-redwood-route headers from the request?

maya_customer: x-request-id: rwd-7f3b2. We do have proxy logs — attaching a small excerpt: 

```
[proxy] 2026-03-16T22:01:02Z rwd-7f3b2 GET /v1/streams/generate 200 0.23s upstream=10.0.5.12:8080 "chunked" bytes=1423 conn=12345
[proxy] 2026-03-16T22:01:03Z rwd-7f3b2 upstream close 502 unexpected reset_by_peer
```

alex_support: Noted. Can you confirm whether you see a 502 on client side or just EOF? Also are you using any intermediate CDN (CloudFront / Fastly) in front of your clients?

maya_customer: Client sees EOF, sometimes an HTTP 502. We do have CloudFront in front. When this happens, re-requesting often returns the full payload. Rate ~1-3/100 requests under peak.

karim_eng: CloudFront can sometimes cut streaming responses if an origin signals reset or if keepalive is hit. Two things to try: 1) enable SSE chunk aggregation in client (reassemble across multiple event chunks) 2) on our side, we should check connection idle timeouts and chunk flush behavior for the structured JSON path. I'll pull gw/nginx and app logs for rwd-7f3b2 and check for any forced socket close.

jules_prod: Add to that: structured json mode sometimes emits many small events (one per token / small object). If a proxy has a small write buffer it may flush partial JSON objects. We should ensure the emitter doesn't cut objects across event boundaries — or include a small framing wrapper: send complete JSON objects per SSE event, or send length-prefixed frames. Short-term mitigation: set Content-Length or increase buffer window.

alex_support: For repro hygiene, @maya_customer can you try the same curl but with keepalive disabled on CloudFront or bypass CF (direct to api) for a few minutes and share whether the truncation stops? That narrows down CDN vs origin. Also please open a support ticket with request-id rwd-7f3b2 and attach your client logs.

maya_customer: Will try bypassing CF and report back. If we can't bypass, is there a recommended client-side parsing strategy? Our consumer library assumes a single JSON array per stream and fails when it gets mid-array chunk.

karim_eng: Recommended parsing: treat the stream as a sequence of SSE 'data' payloads and stitch them together before attempting to parse the resulting JSON. Don't assume single-HTTP-body atomicity. Example pseudo:

```js
let buffer = '';
source.onmessage = (evt) => {
  buffer += evt.data;
  try {
    const parsed = JSON.parse(buffer);
    handle(parsed);
    buffer = '';
  } catch(e) {
    // wait for more chunks
  }
};
```

That handles chunk boundaries. We'll also investigate server-side to prevent emitting partial objects if possible.

ingest-proxy-bot: trace: sock-reset 1958000020 upstream=10.0.5.12 code=RST_REASON_KEEPALIVE_TIMEOUT

jules_prod: Filing internal follow-up: PROD-STREAM-JSON-195800 — check origin keepalive config, streaming flush threshold, and SSE framing for structured mode. Also verify the streaming SDK docs emphasize client reassembly.

alex_support: Thanks everyone. @maya_customer please post results of the direct-to-origin test. If truncation persists after bypassing CDN we'll escalate to infra on-call and request tcpdump from your side for the failing flow. :thumbsup:

maya_customer: Bypassed CF and reproduced same EOF twice. Attached tcpdump (shared privately). Looks like origin closed after sending partial chunk. Thanks — please escalate to infra.

karim_eng: Got the pcap, thanks. Initial look shows FIN from origin immediately after partial chunk when memory spike occurs in the generator process. Suspect a backpressure/oom edge-case in the structured serializer. I'll open a diagnostic branch to replicate locally with the same payload size pattern. Will post follow-up here.

alex_support: Escalation created to eng-infra and eng-runtime with link: https://redwood-internal/bugs/PROD-STREAM-JSON-195800. Keeping thread open for updates.

maya_customer: Appreciate it. Customer impact: failing JSON parse causes feature rollback for affected users — ~2% of sessions. Please prioritize.

karim_eng: Understood. Prioritizing. Preliminary mitigation: add server-side flush coalescing and make serializer emit complete objects per SSE event. ETA for hotfix: 48h. Will update thread with patch and deploy plan.

alex_support: Closing loop: created support ticket 78945 and attached logs. Will notify customer once hotfix is staged. :white_check_mark:
